question: On Friday, 9 February, a gang of drug traffickers murdered two Guardia Civil officers and seriously injured two others in the port of Barbate (Cádiz). According to video footage, the drug traffickers’ speedboat attacked the Guardia Civil's inflatable patrol vessel by ramming it. The criminals clearly had the upper hand in terms of equipment.

On 16 September 2022 the Ministry of the Interior disbanded the Guardia Civil’s OCON Sur anti-drug trafficking task force after four years of successful work. In the meantime, drug trafficking is gaining ground in Spain’s ports. The Commissioner for Home Affairs, Ylva Johansson, has already expressed concern at this. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider that the Spanish Government needs to provide greater resources to combat drug trafficking in Spanish ports?
Does the Commission consider disbanding the OCON Sur task force to be well advised given the increase in organised crime in Spanish ports?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.4.2024) The Commission is concerned with the increase of drug-related violence across Europe and condemns the recent tragic event in Barbate. Member States hold exclusive competencies for the internal allocation of resources and the establishment or dissolution of specialised task forces. The Commission supports Member States in their fight against drug trafficking.

In particular, the Commission, alongside the EU agencies and Member States, actively implements the EU Drugs Strategy1 and Action Plan 2021-20252. As a part of these activities, a new EU Drugs Agency3, with an upgraded mandate, will replace the European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction (EMCDDA) as of July 2024.

Europol’s mandate was also strengthened in 2022 to better support Member States in combating organised crime. More recently, the Commission adopted a comprehensive EU roadmap to address drug trafficking and organised crime4, which includes priority actions to be implemented by the Commission but also by Member States in order to strengthen the resilience of logistic hubs – in particular ports.

The launch of the European Ports Alliance in January 20245 was a key action contributing to stepping up the cooperation with law enforcement in ports. This work will be supported by the results of the Schengen evaluation on drugs trafficking, concluded in November 2023.
